sections.h2: Which Brandenburg offices matter for a Meade County tax bill?
sections.html:
Most of the work happens in two suites at 516 Hillcrest Drive. Suite 3 is home to the Property Valuation Administration (PVA), reachable at (270) 422-2178 Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. until half past four. Suite 14 is the Sheriff's Office, where payments are taken, at (270) 422-4937.

Value is one office's business and collection is the other's. Take exemption and value questions to Suite 3, and take a bill in hand to Suite 14. The County Clerk becomes involved only after April 15, once unpaid bills have transferred.

sections.h2: How and when do Meade County residents pay?
sections.html:
Pay the Sheriff. The Sheriff mailed the 2026 bills on October 30, 2026, a Friday, and a notice dated November 4 conceded that many owners still had not received theirs. It directed them to an online lookup of 2026 tax information so the amount could be checked while the mail caught up.

  • Statute KRS 134.015 allows a 2 percent discount if the bill is paid by November 1. Because the 2026 bills only left October 30, ask the Sheriff which dates apply; the law permits a different schedule when mailing is delayed.
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount.
  • January brings 5 percent.
  • After January it is 10 percent.
  • April 15 ends collection, and in 2026 the counter took its last in-person payment at 4:30 p.m.

Late payers should know that personal checks are refused for the last two weeks of each collection season. The workable choices then are cash, a card, a money order or a cashier's check. The office describes this as a yearly custom, with personal checks accepted again earlier in future seasons.

sections.h2: What does a typical Meade County house owe?
sections.html:
Census reports $207,900 for a middle-of-the-road owned home, more than McCracken County's $188,100. Frankfort's 2025 rate, 10.6 cents per $100, means about $220.37 for the state on such a house. The county, the school district and special districts levy separately and are added. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,344, and those without one report $462.

Population nearly doubled between 1950 and 1960, then kept rising:

An estimated 30,699 people lived here in July 2025, up 2.3 percent on 2020. Typical rent is $1,026, typical household income $74,355, and 165 building permits were issued in 2025. Jobs at employer establishments rose 6.2 percent over the 2022 to 2023 period to 3,633 across 362 firms, and retail sales reached about $305 million in 2022.

Census counts 11,007 households averaging 2.72 people, in a stock of 12,666 housing units. Some 87.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, a lower share than in McLean or McCreary counties. Persons without health insurance under 65 make up 7.4 percent, and the median age at the 2020 census was 38.4, with 25.5 percent of residents under 18.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Meade County?
sections.html:
Yes. For 2025 and 2026 the state lets owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, take $49,100 off assessed value. On the $207,900 median, $158,800 stays taxable and the state's portion falls to roughly $168.33.

For the 2026 tax year, the Meade County PVA gave May 22 as the filing date for the exemption to appear on the November bill, which is now behind us. An owner turning 65 in a later year should ask the office for that year's date. The PVA adds that early filing helps the taxing districts plan. Proof of age can be a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claims need a finding of total disability and a renewal every year, with service-connected veterans and permanent Social Security or state-retirement findings excused from renewing.

sections.h2: How does a Meade County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
Before anything is filed, visit the PVA for the required conference, where staff walk through how your value was built. Then keep to the state's calendar:

  • The roll can be viewed for 13 days starting the first Monday in May.
  • File at the County Clerk's office by closing time on the next business day after viewing ends.
  • Bring documents on the land and buildings, such as insurance papers, construction costs and sale listings.
  • Appear before the local board of assessment appeals, which meets about a month after viewing and may sit up to five days.

The hearing may be recorded by you. If the board's number ends up above your claim after bills have gone out, you will be sent a supplemental bill for the gap.

sections.h2: What if Meade County tax is still owed when the house sells?
sections.html:
Closing does not erase it. The County Clerk takes a bill still open on April 15 as a certificate, files a lien, and charges 1 percent a month. KRS 134.420 lets that lien last 11 years under any owner.

The county attorney mails two notices, one inside 30 days of the transfer and another inside 60. A sale is set 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the buyer of a certificate may add substantial fees. Get a payoff from the Sheriff until April 15 and from the Clerk after, and let the closing agent pay it from proceeds.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Meade County?
sections.html:
Created in 1823, Meade County covers 325 square miles, and the Ohio River runs along its 56-mile northern line, facing Indiana. Karst plains riddled with sinkholes cover much of the land, while the northwest rests on a plateau behind the Dripping Springs Escarpment. Brandenburg is the seat. Ekron and Muldraugh are the county's other cities, with Doe Valley and Fort Knox counted as census-designated places. Hardin County shares Fort Knox, and Meade is part of the Louisville metro area, within easy reach of the job centers at Elizabethtown and Fort Knox.

Meade County Schools, with Meade County High School, teaches most children. Families living on the Fort Knox base are zoned to the Defense Department's schools instead. Eastern time applies here, while neighbors Breckinridge County and Perry County, Indiana, are on Central.

Workers travel a mean 33.0 minutes to their jobs. Owners live in 74.1 percent of homes, and 91.5 percent of households have broadband. The Census lists 2,790 veterans, 17.4 percent of residents at 65 or older, and a 91.0 percent high school graduation rate among adults. Poverty stands at 9.8 percent, against 13.9 percent in McCracken County. Sinkholes are common in this terrain, and a house with one or with deferred repairs can stall a conventional sale. Cash buyers who take a house as-is can close without those fixes.

faqs.q: Where do I pay the Meade County Sheriff?
faqs.a: Go to 516 Hillcrest Drive, Suite 14, in Brandenburg, or call (270) 422-4937. The PVA, in Suite 3, does not take payments.

faqs.q: When does the Meade County Sheriff stop taking personal checks?
faqs.a: For the last two weeks before April 15. Cash, cards, money orders and cashier's checks remain acceptable.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 homestead filing cutoff in Meade County?
faqs.a: May 22, 2026, in order for the exemption to appear on the November bill. That has passed, so ask the PVA for the next cutoff.

faqs.q: How much state tax falls on a $207,900 Meade County house?
faqs.a: Close to $220.37 on the state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100, before county and school levies.

faqs.q: What becomes of Meade County bills left open after April 15?
faqs.a: The County Clerk receives them as certificates of delinquency. A lien is filed, interest runs at 1 percent a month, and a sale may be set 90 to 135 days after the move.
